raw_response:
I am not going to spread myself too much this year. We only have 24 mu, just 2 people at home, and some family labor is away earning cash, so I have to farm in a steady way, not chase anything fancy. The wheat-maize land is what keeps grain coming, so I will keep most of the land in that rotation. Cotton can bring money, but it takes more watching and more hand work, so I will not put too much area there. I will do 16 mu in wheat then summer maize after harvest, and 8 mu in cotton.

For wheat, I still plant around the usual time in October. If you miss the season, the stand is not good, so I do not play with that. I use the seed I know, not expensive special seed. Fertilizer, I would rather not cut too much. If wheat turns yellow and thin, the loss is bigger than saving a little money on fertilizer. So I put base fertilizer before sowing, then one topdress around jointing. Water from the well is costly, but wheat in our place usually needs a few turns, so I plan about 3 irrigations unless spring rain is good.

After wheat harvest, maize has to go in quickly, almost no waiting. That is why I keep the tillage simple, just harvest wheat, clear the field, and get maize planted fast. I use hybrid maize seed because that is what people around here use and it gives steadier ears. I put one base fertilizer and one chasing fertilizer when the maize is knee-high to waist-high. If rain is normal, maybe 1 irrigation is enough; if it stays dry, I may add another, but I will watch the pumping money.

Cotton I keep on 8 mu only. Cotton can sell for cash, but it needs more labor for pest watching and picking. With only 2 people, I cannot make cotton too big or I will be rushed. I use the kind of seed I can buy nearby, put moderate fertilizer, and irrigate 2 times if needed. Cotton pests can come hard, so I will spray when I see the problem, not blindly too many times.
